query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a 5 μm thick Al2O3 coating to the surface of Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy in the cast state will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Applying a 5 μm thick Al2O3 coating
generation.conditions: Temperature: up to 1000 °C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: 500 hours, Mechanical-loading boundaries: strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.structural_mediator: Al2O3 coating acting as a diffusion barrier
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 coating reduces oxygen diffusion into the alloy, thereby minimizing oxidation and degradation of mechanical properties, as supported by previous studies on the effectiveness of Al2O3 coatings as oxygen diffusion barriers [no specific records provided]
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in oxidation-induced mass gain relative to the uncoated alloy, with no significant change in yield strength (within 10% of the baseline value of 163-530 MPa), based on estimates from similar coating systems
generation.boundary: Temperature: up to 1100 °C, Exposure time: 500 hours
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the Al2O3 coating may vary depending on factors such as coating thickness, surface roughness, and environmental conditions. Additionally, the long-term stability of the coating and its potential degradation over time are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated alloy exhibits a mass gain greater than 20% relative to the uncoated alloy, or a yield strength reduction greater than 10% relative to the baseline value, the hypothesis is falsified
